facts.label: New request
facts.description: New request in three steps (For with Source from, Equipment, Review) on the Future page pattern: v = fxRequests.form(state, form), set by loadChain on vbEnter and on every fxRefresh, and by formChain on every change of the form (it only reads the store); Submit runs createRequest through actChain, which opens the new request's tab; the units offered export through exportChain (docs/redesign/BUILDING-FUTURE-SCREENS.md).

sections: 1 · Who and what it is for
Sourcing business unit: who lends the equipment
fields: e.g. with an operator, or access from the north gate

chains.name: actChain
chains.about: Every action on this page through fxPage.act. Submit (data-act="createRequest") sends the form as fxRequests.payload builds it; fxPage.act toasts what happened and opens the new request's tab (its result names it). Then the form starts again for the same BU. When the engine refuses, its words stay on the page (failure) and nothing changes.

chains.name: exportChain
chains.about: Exports the units offered for the class and dates, as shown (owner, relationship, price, estimate, why not).

chains.name: exportMenuChain
chains.about: Opens or closes the export menu.

chains.name: formChain
chains.about: A choice on the form (the BU, the sourcing BU of Source from or "Show every company", what it is for, the task, the dates, the class, a unit added or removed, a step): the form changes and the steps are shown again. Reads the store only; Submit (actChain) is what raises the request.

chains.name: loadChain
chains.about: New request's view model: fxRequests.form(state, form), the three steps for the persona played (their BUs, the sourcing BUs they may borrow from, projects or customers, the units sourcing offers). Runs on vbEnter and on every fxRefresh (another persona, the demo clock, another booking); replaces v, never mutates it. Writes nothing to the store.

chains.name: openChain
chains.about: Open what a clicked element names in its tab: data-nav="<navId>", or data-record="request" data-id data-number.

modules.name: future/fxPage
modules.about: What every EquipRite Future screen shares (docs/redesign/BUILDING-FUTURE-SCREENS.md): watch(context) in the page module's constructor: the page hears every change to the store (this tab, another tab, the shell's persona switch and demo clock) as its 'fxRefresh' event, whose listener runs loadChain again. Stops by itself when VB disposes the page (its tab closed). view(name, ...args) for loadChain: the screen's view model (fxViews), with ready: true (or error/missing). act(request) for…

modules.name: exportKit
modules.about: Export for every list in EquipRite Next: CSV, Excel (.xlsx), PDF (the print dialog, Save as PDF) and Copy (tab-separated, pastes into Excel or an email). Exactly what the list shows: its filter, its columns, its order. No library: the .xlsx is written here (a zip of the Office Open XML parts, stored, with CRC-32). Columns: [{ key, label, value?: (row) => any, type?: 'text' | 'number' }]. A column's value is value(row) when given, else row[key]. Numbers stay numbers in Excel; everything else is…

modules.name: shellBus
modules.about: How a screen inside a tab talks to the shell around it: open a screen or a record in a tab, name its own tab, show a toast. Each tab is its own flow under oj-vb-switcher, so this one module (loaded once) is the line between them: the shell registers itself; requests made before it has are queued. bus.open({ navId: 'requests' }) bus.open({ record: 'request', params: { id: 10482, number: 'REQ-10482' } }) bus.rename('request:10482', 'REQ-10482') bus.toast('3 rows copied', 'info')

modules.name: future/fxStore
modules.about: EquipRite Future's store: the simulated backend's state. One state, changed only by act(), read by view(). Screens subscribe and refresh when anything changes (in this tab, another tab, or a restored snapshot). Where the story is kept: - in the desktop app: DuckDB in the app's data folder (desktop/lib/futureDb.js, /__future/*): every change is saved there, with the last 50 saves and named snapshots, and the story as SQL tables; - always also in this browser (localStorage), so it opens at once…

No page codes and no feature flags: Future runs on the simulated store (resources/js/future/fxStore.js) alone. Item: id the tab id of the screen (also the navId of fxViews.work() items and of notification links) roles persona roles that see it (any one is enough);…

modules.name: future/fxSeed
modules.about: EquipRite Future: the demo group (FDD v2.0). Three legal entities in two countries: FleetCo (UAE) holds the fleet (Company 2) and rents to its own customers; ProjectCo (UAE) does projects (Company 1), with a second BU (Facilities) in the same legal entity that owns a few units of its own, so own-fleet (SAME_BU) and cross-charge (SAME_LE) cases exist too; ProjectCo Arabia (KSA) does projects across the border (IC_CROSS_BORDER). modules.name: future/fxEngine
modules.about: EquipRite Future: the simulated backend (FDD v2.0). Pure functions on a plain state object; the store (fxStore.js) keeps the state and calls apply(). modules.name: future/fxViews
modules.about: EquipRite Future: what each screen shows, computed from the state for the person being played (MC-BR-12: requests by the requesting BU, approvals by the sourcing BU, finance by legal entity). Pure functions.

modules.name: future/fxReturn
modules.about: EquipRite Future · the return on a date, the final timesheet and the final bill (Receive, hours, moves and a request's Money tab). The engine stops a hire on a date (offHire { date }: today or earlier stops it that day, a later day is a planned return that happens by itself) and takes the final timesheet in one go (logHoursBulk).
